HOW TO READ THESE NUMBERS: METHODOLOGY AND CAVEATS

Monthly figures use the unchanged RBI Database on Indian Economy (DBIE) Report 19 export retrieved October 25, 2026. The ACTUALS rows contain US dollars despite the measure column's display-unit label. We divide by one million for USD millions and aggregate April-March for fiscal years. FY26 means April 2025-March 2026; FY27's latest comparison covers only April-August 2026.

The raw export contains 222 distinct date strings, but only 221 calendar months: six identical category rows dated May 30, 2009 repeat rows dated May 31. We keep one identical value per month and category and reject conflicting duplicates. Three early donation cells are blank; the family/gifts composite omits those months rather than turning the blanks into measured zeros.

An independent reconciliation checks every numeric artifact cell against source CSV coordinates. Of the annual Report 752 cells compared with monthly sums, all but the FY2008-09 total agree at the displayed precision: that annual total is $124.6 million, against $808.1 million from the monthly record. The annual purpose components agree with the monthly aggregate; the disputed headline equals March alone. We use the monthly record consistently and disclose the conflict. We do not claim the two raw exports match throughout.

The education-travel and combined-education series begin in March 2026, when both components are observable. The reported Rs 50 lakh line is a reference benchmark across the valuation chart, not a historical limit. There was no LRS TCS threshold before its introduction, so its line begins in October 2020. External-sector comparisons use the frozen RBI DBIE annual BoP and monthly reserve extracts. All values describe that frozen vintage.

A fresh direct download from RBI reproduced the frozen monthly and annual records and the original external-sector observations. Original responses and refresh receipts are retained with the source-cell audit.
